verdict.summary: Any owner, admin or manager on a Klaviyo account can create an OAuth app in a few minutes. Anyone can install it from its installation URL without review, but each installer sees a 'not reviewed by Klaviyo' warning. Removing that warning and getting listed in the App Marketplace is the hard part: you need at least 5 real customer installs, the registration and security forms, a testing doc, an architecture diagram, a demo, and a security review with no published turnaround time.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min to connect your own account; several days of work (forms, docs, install/uninstall handling, listing assets) for Marketplace submission
verdict.approval_wait: none to connect users (they see an unreviewed-app warning); Marketplace review turnaround is not published

gates.name: Your own OAuth app (unreviewed)
gates.unlocks: You create the app in Manage apps and connect your own Klaviyo account through Composio.
limits: Only owner, admin and manager roles can create OAuth apps
The client secret is shown only once. Regenerating it breaks existing connections.
Access tokens last about 1 hour (rely on expires_in). A refresh token unused for 90 days expires.

gates.name: Unlisted install via installation URL
gates.unlocks: You share the OAuth installation URL with testers and customers. They can install and use the app without a Marketplace listing.
limits: Every installer sees an OAuth warning that Klaviyo has not reviewed the app
No install or user cap is documented for unreviewed apps
Before you can submit for review, you need at least 5 active customer installs with production API activity. Developer and company accounts do not count.
Tokens are issued per Klaviyo account, not per user

gates.name: Approved App Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: Klaviyo removes the unreviewed-app warning and customers can find the app in the App Marketplace. Public installs via URL already work without this step.
limits: The Integration registration form and a per-app Security form are mandatory
The app must pass Klaviyo's security review
Klaviyo can decline to list an app for any reason
Changes to listing content need re-review
gates.time_to_reach: Unknown. You first need 5 real installs, then Klaviyo's review time, which is not published.

steps.title: Confirm your Klaviyo role
steps.detail: Sign in to the Klaviyo account that will own the app and confirm your role is owner, admin or manager. Other roles cannot create OAuth apps. The Manage apps page requires a login.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app
steps.detail: Go to Manage apps, click Create app, and enter a name. Copy the client ID and client secret into a secrets manager, then click Create. On the confirmation page, click Continue.
gotchas: The client secret is shown only once. You can generate a new one later, but that breaks every connection that uses the old secret.
Keep the secret server-side and never put it in browser code.

steps.title: Pick the minimum scope set
steps.detail: List every Klaviyo endpoint your agent calls and look up the scope each one needs in its API reference (for example, creating a list needs lists:write). Always keep accounts:read. Composio's default list has about 34 scopes, many of them write scopes. Cut it down to what you actually use, because Klaviyo rejects apps that request more scopes than they need.
gotchas: A reporting-only app should request only read scopes.

steps.title: Enter scopes and redirect URL in the app's OAuth settings
steps.detail: In the app's OAuth settings, enter your scopes as a space-separated list and add the redirect URL, then save. Separate multiple redirect URLs with a space, tab or newline. The redirect URI must exactly match the one Composio sends.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Scopes
values.value: accounts:read plus only the scopes your endpoints need, space-separated

gotchas: Composio's catalog default callback is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but the probe used /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Copy the exact URL from your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Create a custom OAuth2 auth config in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Klaviyo auth config using OAuth2 with your own client ID and secret, and use the same trimmed scope list you entered in Klaviyo. Klaviyo's token endpoint is a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token. Token and revoke calls sent through www.klaviyo.com are blocked.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio and approve it in Klaviyo, then make one API call (for example, to an accounts endpoint) to confirm it works. Klaviyo requires PKCE (S256) and the authorization code expires in 5 minutes, so the code must be exchanged promptly.
gotchas: Access tokens last about 1 hour. Use expires_in rather than a hardcoded value.
A refresh token that goes unused for 90 days expires, and the customer must reauthorize.

steps.title: Share the installation URL with testers and customers
steps.detail: Send the OAuth installation URL directly to customers. You don't need a listing for this. They will see an unreviewed-app warning but can install and use the app. If you plan to submit to the Marketplace, collect at least 5 real customer installs with live API activity. Your own accounts and company-associated accounts do not count.

steps.title: Make the install and uninstall flow pass review
steps.detail: Make sure the installation URL starts the OAuth flow directly and works from klaviyo.com, from any klaviyo.com subdomain, and from your own app. Handle errors: show a dismissible message when a user denies permissions, and a session-expired message that restarts installation when the code has expired. Provide an in-app disconnect that revokes the refresh token, and reflect uninstalls made from Klaviyo in your app.
gotchas: Klaviyo rejects apps for avoidable manual install steps, for install URLs that land on a website or integrations page, and for an API-key connection that remains after moving to OAuth.

steps.title: Complete the registration and security forms and accept the partner terms
steps.detail: In the Registration & security tab, submit the Integration registration form (once per company) and the Security form (once per app). Accept the Technology Partner Agreement, the Acceptable Use Policy and the API Terms of Use. Before you answer the security form, confirm your systems meet Klaviyo's security standards.
gotchas: If you submit without both forms, the app is rejected.

The security standards require TLS 1.2 or higher, OAuth tokens encrypted at rest, secrets kept in a secrets manager, MFA, audit logs kept for at least 365 days, and fixes for critical or high-severity dependency vulnerabilities within 3 or 7 days.

steps.title: Draft listing content and testing materials
steps.detail: Draft the listing text: developer name (30 characters or fewer), primary category, short description (75 or fewer), full description (300 or fewer), and 2-6 key features. Collect the website, privacy policy, terms of service, pricing and support URLs, and a 48x48 SVG logo. Adapt Klaviyo's testing template into a Google Doc with Commenter access. It must cover the customer workflow, each endpoint with its use case and scope, an architecture diagram, and how to test the OAuth flow end to end.
gotchas: Klaviyo does not accept public documentation links in place of the testing doc, and you must not send account credentials.
Your public website needs a demo video, step-by-step setup docs and at least one user guide.

steps.title: Record the demo and submit for review
steps.detail: Record the demo video. Then open the app's three-dot menu, choose Edit, and complete the Authentication, Company details and Listing details sections. Click Review submission, check the section statuses, and click Submit.

steps.title: Wait for Klaviyo's review email
steps.detail: Klaviyo emails you when the app is approved, rejected, or needs changes. Klaviyo does not publish a turnaround time. Approval removes the unreviewed-app warning and makes the app discoverable in the Marketplace.

steps.title: Maintain the app after approval
steps.detail: Scope changes on a published app apply automatically without resubmission, but existing installs keep their old scopes until users reauthorize. Changes to listing content need re-review before they go live. Check API usage and error rates in the Insights tab, because high error rates can get the app delisted.

requirements.item: Owner, admin or manager role on the Klaviyo account
requirements.detail: Needed to create the OAuth app.

requirements.item: Redirect URI exactly matching an allowlisted URL
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri in the authorize and token requests must match an allowlist entry exactly.
Installs must show production API activity. Developer and company accounts do not count.

requirements.item: Integration registration form, per-app Security form, and acceptance of partner terms
requirements.detail: Covers the Technology Partner Agreement, the Acceptable Use Policy and the API Terms of Use. Submitting without the forms means rejection.

TLS 1.2 or higher, OAuth tokens encrypted at rest, secrets kept in a secrets manager, expiring tokens, MFA, audit logs kept for at least 365 days, and critical or high vulnerabilities fixed within 3 or 7 days.
Company name, description, website and contact email. Developer name (30 characters or fewer), category, short description (75 or fewer), full description (300 or fewer), and 2-6 key features.
Website, privacy policy, terms of service, pricing and support URLs, plus a 48x48 SVG logo with no scripting. If you choose the multi-media type, add a gallery of 4-8 images.

requirements.item: Public website with demo video, setup docs and user guide
requirements.detail: The website must explain the app's benefits and include current visuals.

requirements.item: Testing doc as a Google Doc with Commenter access
requirements.detail: An adapted copy of Klaviyo's testing template, with the customer workflow, endpoints with their use cases and scopes, an architecture diagram, a demo, and end-to-end OAuth testing details. Do not include credentials.

The install URL starts OAuth directly and works from klaviyo.com, its subdomains, and your app. Denied-permission and expired-code errors are handled. Uninstalls from your app revoke the refresh token.

scopes.effect: Required for every app. Never remove it.

scopes.scope: *:write scopes (campaigns, flows, lists, profiles, events, etc.)
scopes.effect: There is no separate scope review, but request write scopes only for endpoints you actually call. Klaviyo rejects over-scoped apps at review.
A reporting-only app should request only read scopes. Map each endpoint to the scope named in its API reference.
Needed only for the beta Applications API, which returns an app's status, scopes and callback URLs. Not needed for normal integrations.

blockers.symptom: Token or revoke requests fail after migrating code or using an old base URL
blockers.cause: Since March 31, 2025, Klaviyo blocks oauth/token and oauth/revoke traffic routed through www.klaviyo.com.
blockers.fix: Send token and revoke calls to https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token and https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/revoke.

blockers.cause: The callback URL Composio sends doesn't exactly match an allowlisted redirect URL.
blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into the app's redirect URLs in Manage apps and save.

blockers.cause: The app requests more scopes than it uses, for example Composio's full default list.
blockers.fix: Request only the scopes named in the API reference of each endpoint you call, plus accounts:read.

blockers.symptom: Cannot submit, or submission is rejected right away
blockers.cause: Fewer than 5 qualifying customer installs, or the registration and security forms are missing.
blockers.fix: Get real customer installs through the installation URL, and complete both forms in the Registration & security tab before submitting.

blockers.cause: The install URL lands on a website instead of the OAuth flow, there is no in-app disconnect, Klaviyo-side uninstall is still a separate step, or an API-key connection remains.
blockers.fix: Fix the install and uninstall flow as described in Klaviyo's 'pass your app review' guidance, and re-test before submitting.
Avoid regenerating the secret. If you must, update Composio right away and have users reconnect.

blockers.cause: The customer uninstalled the app, the token was revoked, or the refresh token went unused for more than 90 days.
blockers.fix: Mark the connection as disconnected and ask the customer to reauthorize.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Klaviyo. Your options are your own OAuth app (OAuth2 auth config) or an API key. To use OAuth, register your own app and add Composio's callback URL to its redirect allowlist. Copy the exact callback from your auth config: the catalog default is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback was also seen. Composio's default list has about 34 scopes, many of them write scopes. Trim it to the scopes your agent uses, because Klaviyo rejects over-scoped apps. Authorize URL: https://www.klaviyo.com/oauth/authorize. Token URL: https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token.

open_questions: Klaviyo does not publish a review turnaround time anywhere in the pages reviewed.
No install or user cap is documented for unreviewed or unlisted apps. Only the 5-install minimum for submission is stated.
Which Composio callback URL applies (/api/v1/auth-apps/add or /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback)? Copy it from your auth config.
Whether Klaviyo accepts localhost, http, or wildcard redirect URIs is not documented beyond the exact-match rule.
Whether the refresh token rotates on each refresh is not clearly documented.
The refresh endpoint's 10-calls-per-minute limit comes only from a third-party blog and is unverified.
When a user disconnects through Composio, does Composio call Klaviyo's revoke endpoint? Klaviyo's review requires uninstalls from the app side to revoke the refresh token.
Account prerequisites beyond the owner/admin/manager role (free vs paid plan, identity verification) are not documented.
